'''Denise Marie Barthomeuf''' (26 November 1934 – 2 November 2004) was a French chemist. She was known for her pioneering research on the structure of the [[Zeolite|zeolites]] mineral group. She created models to demonstrate the structure of zeolites and facilitate understanding of their use as catalysts. She founded and led the organisation dedicated to zeolites. In 2026, Barthomeuf was announced as one of women in STEM whose names are destined to be added to the [[List of the 72 names on the Eiffel Tower|72 men]] already celebrated on the [[Eiffel Tower]]. 

== Early life and education ==
Denise Marie Barthomeuf was born to Madeleine (née Gallet) and Jean Baptiste Barthomeuf on 26 November 1934 in [[Lyon]].<ref name=":2">{{Cite web |title=matchID – Moteur de recherche des décès |url=https://deces.matchid.io/id/tYUSrpcYzUKb |access-date=2025-03-01 |website=deces.matchid.io}}</ref> She took her degree in science at the [[University of Lyon]] in 1960 and her Ph.D in Chemistry in 1962 under the supervision of Marcel Prettre.<ref name=":0" />
[[File:Natrolite_-_Monzoni,_Val_di_Fassa,_Italia_01.jpg|thumb|250x250px|Example of a zeolite.]]

== Career ==
In 1958, Barthomeuf began her career at the [[Claude Bernard University Lyon 1|Faculté des sciences de Lyon]] as an assistant in Professor Marcel Prettre's laboratory. She was promoted to senior assistant in 1964.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |last=Société chimique de France |title=Hommage – Denise Barthomeuf (1934–2004) |url=https://new.societechimiquedefrance.fr/wp-content/uploads/2019/12/H-287.pdf |access-date=13 Feb 2026 |language=fr}}</ref>

Her early years of research focussed on the study of catalytic cracking catalysts. Her first academic contribution was at the International Catalysis Congress in Paris in 1960, where she presented a paper on the influence of several novel physical-chemical properties on the cracking activity of [[Amorphous silica–alumina|silica-alumina catalysts]].<ref>Influence of several novel physical-chemical properties on the cracking activity of silica-alumina catalysts, Actes Intern. Congr. Catalyse, 2 (1960), 1961, 1, p. 1313).</ref>

Whilst her research initially focused on catalytic cracking catalysts, after spending eight months at [[Moscow State University]], in the laboratory run by professor {{Ill|Klawdija Wassiljewna Toptschijewa|de|Klawdija Wassiljewna Toptschijewa}}, she turned her attention to [[Zeolite|zeolites]] in the 1960s.<ref name=":0" /> 

In the later 1960s, Barthomeuf was the first to identify the importance and role of the composition and spatial organisation of the atoms that make up the microporous materials in determining the properties of zeolites. This led her to develop methods for modifying zeolites, which had a strong impact in the field, including the introduction of dealuminated zeolites in catalytic cracking.<ref name=":0" />

Barthomeuf joined the [[French National Centre for Scientific Research]] (CNRS) in 1974.<ref name=":0" /> She also worked in industry for eight years in three different roles, at [[Rhône-Poulenc]]; Liha; then [[ExxonMobil|Exxon]] in the United States where she focused on basic zeolites, aluminophosphates and separation processes.<ref name=":0" /> She worked at three CNRS laboratories: both the Institute for Research on Catalysis and the Organic Catalysis Laboratory in [[Villeurbanne]], and later at the Surface Reactivity Laboratory in Paris.<ref name=":1">[https://10ca8303-b3dc-4a91-9dcc-2d2b91792b47.usrfiles.com/ugd/10ca83_3838bd19a41a4e83927cfc8fe0f50404.pdf 72 femmes de sciences pour la tour Eiffel] ''Femmes & Sciences'' (in French). Retrieved 2026-02-13</ref>

Barthomeuf conceptualised the relationships between the properties of zeolites, their acidity and their catalytic behaviour. In the 1980s, she published a series of articles and lectured on the topological density of aluminium atoms in networks. She developed a predictive model defining the optimum acidity and activity for each structure. She enriched the model, accounting for the existence of electrostatic field gradients within the cavities, and explaining the changes in selectivity in hydrocarbon cracking reactions as a function of pore composition and size. These concepts were integrated into the study of zeolites.<ref name=":0" />

Barthomeuf founded the Groupe français des Zéolithes (GFZ), which she chaired until 1990.<ref name=":0" /> She was vice-chair of the International Zeolite Association and chaired their Breck Award Committee from 1986 to 1989.<ref>{{Cite web |title=IZA Announcements 2004–2005 |url=https://www.iza-online.org/IZA_Ann_2004-2005.htm |access-date=2026-02-13 |website=www.iza-online.org}}</ref>

Her laboratory work and her collaboration with industry in France and the United States significantly contributed to an improved understanding of [[catalysis]] and [[Reactivity (chemistry)|reactivity]], especially in relation to zeolites and other catalytic materials. Together with the mathematician [[Michelle Schatzman]], she was one of two Eiffel Women closely associated with the [[University of Lyon|Univeristy of Lyon I]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.univ-lyon1.fr/actualites/72-noms-de-femmes-scientifiques-dont-deux-de-nos-anciennes-enseignantes-chercheuses-illumineront-bientot-la-tour-eiffel|title=Deux figures de notre université parmi les 72 femmes de science mises à l’honneur sur la Tour Eiffel|publisher=Lyon I Université|date=10 February 2026|access-date=20 June 2026|language=French}}</ref>

== Retirement ==
Barthomeuf retired in 1995 and earned a masters degree in archaeology, developing an interest in the manufacture of early alloys.<ref name=":0" /> She also became involved in archaeology and humanitarian work with disadvantaged communities in Nepal.<ref>''Une action humanitaire pour les habitants de l'Himalaya'', ''Le Progrès'', 5 March 2000</ref><ref name=":1" /> Nevertheless, she continued to write papers on her main interest, zeolites and related minerals. Her last publication, "Si,Al Ordering and Basicity Clusters in Faujasites" appeared in [[Journal of Physical Chemistry]] in December 2004.<ref name=":0"/>

Barthomeuf died aged 69 on 2 November 2004 in [[Saint-Cyr-au-Mont-d'Or]], a suburb of Lyon.<ref name=":2" />

== Honours and awards ==
In 1985, Barthomeuf was awarded the [[CNRS Silver Medal]]<ref>{{Cite web |last=Burgos |first=Valérie |date=2023-01-31 |title=Médailles d’argent du CNRS 1960–2010 |url=https://comihistocnrs.hypotheses.org/2706 |access-date=2026-02-13 |website=Comité pour l'histoire du CNRS |language=fr-FR}}</ref>

Since 2017, the international Denise Barthomeuf Prize has been awarded by the Groupe français de Zéolithes (GFZ) for PhD theses in the field of zeolites or related materials.<ref>{{Cite web |title=39ème réunion annuelle du GFZ - Sciencesconf.org |url=https://gfz2024.sciencesconf.org/resource/page/id/1 |access-date=2026-02-13 |website=gfz2024.sciencesconf.org}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=LCS |date=2021-02-09 |title=Dr. Florent Dubray received the prestigious Denise Barthomeuf Award from the French Zeolite Association (GFZ) |url=https://www.lcs.ensicaen.fr/dr-florent-dubray-received-the-very-prestigious-denise-barthomeuf-award-from-the-french-zeolite-association-gfz/?lang=en |access-date=2026-02-13 |website=Laboratoire Catalyse & Spectrochimie |language=en-US}}</ref> Under the sponsorship of [[Micromeritics]], an award of 400 euros is presented to winners at the annual meeting of the GFZ.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://gfz-online.fr/fr/bourses/pix-de-these|title=Prix de thèse GFZ|publisher=Association GFZ|access-date=19 June 2026}}</ref> 

In 2026, Denise Barthomeuf was announced as one of 72 historical women in STEM whose names have been proposed to be added to the [[List of the 72 names on the Eiffel Tower|72 men]] already celebrated on the [[Eiffel Tower]]. The plan was conceived by a student and tour guide named Bernard Rigaud and it was taken up by Sorbonne University's President [[Nathalie Drach-Temam]].<ref name="rigaud">{{Cite web |title=The Hypatia project: engraving the names of 72 women scientists on the Eiffel Tower |url=https://www.sorbonne-universite.fr/en/news/hypatia-project-engraving-names-72-women-scientists-eiffel-tower |access-date=2026-06-15 |website=Sorbonne Université |language=en}}</ref> and it was announced by the Mayor of Paris, [[Anne Hidalgo]] following the recommendations of a committee led by [[Isabelle Vauglin]] of ''[[Femmes et Sciences]]'' and Jean-François Martins, representing the operating company which runs the Eiffel Tower.<ref>{{citation |title=Eiffel Tower: a list of 72 women scientists will soon be inscribed on the Parisian monument |url=https://www.sortiraparis.com/en/news/in-paris/articles/340564-eiffel-tower-list-of-72-women-scientists-soon-to-be-honored-on-the-paris-landmark |access-date=2026-02-02 |website=www.sortiraparis.com |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{citation |title=Les noms des 72 femmes pour la Tour Eiffel ont été révélés. |url=https://www.femmesetsciences.fr/news/les-noms-des-72-femmes-pour-la-tour-eiffel-ont-%C3%A9t%C3%A9-r%C3%A9v%C3%A9l%C3%A9 |access-date=2026-02-22 |website=Femmes & Sciences |language=fr}}</ref><ref>[https://10ca8303-b3dc-4a91-9dcc-2d2b91792b47.usrfiles.com/ugd/10ca83_3838bd19a41a4e83927cfc8fe0f50404.pdf 72 femmes de sciences pour la tour Eiffel] ''Femmes & Sciences'' (in French). Retrieved 2026-02-22</ref><ref name=":11">{{citation |date=2026-01-26 |title=Eiffel Tower to honor 72 women scientists for posterity |url=https://www.lemonde.fr/en/france/article/2026/01/26/eiffel-tower-to-honor-72-women-in-science-for-posterity_6749828_7.html |access-date=2026-02-03 |language=en}}</ref>

== Selected publications ==

* 1961: ''Influence of several novel physical-chemical properties on the cracking activity of silica-alumina catalysts'', Proceedings Intern. Congr. Catalyse, Paris
* 1962: ''Contribution à l'étude des propriétés acides des gels mixtes silice-alumine'', Lyon, Faculté des sciences de l'université de Lyon.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Barthomeuf |first=D. |last2=Prette |first2=M. |date=1962 |title=Contribution à l'étude des propriétés acides des gels mixtes silice-alumine |url=https://research.ebsco.com/c/gx5tqd/search/details/al6n44fxsf?q=Denise%20Barthomeuf |access-date=30 June 2026 |website=UCBL}}</ref> 
* 1963: ''Contribution à l'étude des gels mixtes silice-alumine''. Lyon, Faculté des sciences de l'université de Lyon.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Barthomeuf |first=D. |date=1963 |title=Contribution à l'étude des gels mixtes silice-alumine |url=https://books.google.pt/books/about/Contribution_%C3%A0_l_%C3%A9tude_des_gels_mixtes.html?id=obPy0QEACAAJ&redir_esc=y |access-date=30 June 2026 |website=Google Books}}</ref>
* 1964: ''Si,Al ordering and basicity clusters in faujasite'', published in the [[Journal of Physical Chemistry]] in December 2004<ref name=":0"/>

Researchgate records 143 publications by Barthomeuf.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Denise Barthomeuf |url=https://www.researchgate.net/scientific-contributions/Denise-Barthomeuf-72507380 |website=Researchgate}}</ref>
